docs.title: CodeGuard
docs.text:
Static analysis that finds security anti-patterns in source code — fast, offline, and built to sit at every gate of your workflow (editor, pre-commit, pre-push, PR/CI, merge, scheduled audit) from a single config file.

Status: alpha, heading to v2.0

Today CodeGuard scans Python with five security rules. The v2.0 line adds JavaScript and TypeScript, a config file, baseline/diff scanning, a CI-native command, and packaged distribution (pre-commit hook, GitHub Action, Docker image, standalone binaries). Public interfaces are not yet stable — see Migrating to v2.

docs.title: What it produces
docs.text:
Each finding carries a stable rule ID, a severity, a CWE/OWASP mapping, a precise location, and a plain-English fix suggestion. Output is human-readable text, JSON, or SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning.

myproject/auth.py:12:5  [CG-SEC-001] HIGH  SQL query built with string formatting
    12 | cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {uid}")
         ^
  → Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("SELECT ... WHERE id = %s", (uid,))

1 finding(s)  (1 high)

docs.title: Rules today
docs.text:
ID Catches Severity CWE CG-SEC-001 SQL built with f-strings / % / .format() / concat HIGH CWE-89 CG-SEC-002 Hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens HIGH CWE-798 CG-SEC-003 eval() / exec() / compile() on non-literal input HIGH CWE-95 CG-SEC-004 pickle / marshal / yaml.load without a safe loader HIGH CWE-502 CG-SEC-005 subprocess(..., shell=True) with a dynamic command HIGH CWE-78

See Rules overview.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
discovery  →  language adapter (parse)  →  rules (analyze)  →  findings
                                                                  │
                          suppressions · baseline · severity  ────┤
                                                                  ▼
                              formatter (human · json · sarif · …)

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• engine/registry.py — RuleRegistry, the catalogue of rules. Rules self-register at import time; duplicate IDs are a hard error. The module-level REGISTRY singleton is what the runner uses.
  • engine/rule.py — the Rule base class. A rule detects exactly one concern, is self-contained, and holds no state between files.
  • engine/finding.py — Finding, Location, Severity, Category. Finding is a frozen dataclass and the atomic unit of output.
  • engine/runner.py — AnalysisRunner walks the filesystem, parses each file, runs the active rules, applies suppressions, and returns findings.
  • cli/ — the codeguard command (click) and the output formatters.
  • rules/ — built-in rules, grouped by category. Each is one file plus a vulnerable/safe fixture pair under tests/fixtures/.

docs.title: v2.0 additions
docs.text:
• lang/ — a language adapter layer. LanguageSupport implementations wrap a parser (stdlib ast for Python; tree-sitter for JavaScript and TypeScript) and hand rules a uniform SourceNode. Rules declare the languages they target.
  • config/ — config discovery, schema, and monorepo nearest-wins merging.
  • engine/discovery.py — .gitignore-aware file discovery with parallel scanning.
  • engine/fingerprint.py — stable finding fingerprints for baseline and SARIF.
  • engine/suppressions.py — language-aware suppression parsing with reasons and expiry.

The Rule → Finding contract and the RuleRegistry pattern are unchanged in shape; the rule method is renamed check → analyze(ctx) and takes a context object instead of a bare ast tree.

docs.title: GitHub Actions (today)
docs.text:
- name: Run CodeGuard
  run: |
    pip install codeguard-cli
    codeguard scan src/ --format sarif -o codeguard.sarif || true

- name: Upload SARIF
  uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: codeguard.sarif

Findings then appear in the repository's Security → Code scanning tab and as annotations on pull requests.

docs.title: v2.0
docs.text:
• codeguard ci — scans only files changed since the merge-base, applies a baseline, emits SARIF plus inline PR annotations.
  • .pre-commit-hooks.yaml — codeguard (fast, changed files), codeguard-full (pre-push), codeguard-ci (manual).
  • codeguard-action — a Marketplace action wrapping the above.
  • Docker image — ghcr.io/mevichitra/codeguard.
  • Standalone binaries — attached to each GitHub release.

See Exit codes for gating and Configuration for the shared config file.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Arrives in v2.0

Config-file support is not yet implemented. Today, configure a run with CLI flags (see Usage). This page describes the planned v2.0 model.

docs.title: File
docs.text:
CodeGuard reads codeguard.toml from the project root, or a [tool.codeguard] table in pyproject.toml. In a monorepo the nearest config to each scanned file wins, merged with configs above it.

[tool.codeguard]
include    = ["src/**", "lib/**"]
exclude    = ["**/*.min.js", "tests/fixtures/**"]
languages  = ["python", "javascript", "typescript"]
fail_on    = "high"        # minimum severity that yields exit 1
gitignore  = true
baseline   = ".codeguard-baseline.json"

[tool.codeguard.rules]
disable = ["CG-SEC-002"]

[tool.codeguard.rules.CG-SEC-002]
severity = "medium"

[[tool.codeguard.overrides]]
path    = "migrations/**"
disable = ["CG-SEC-001"]

Validate it with codeguard validate. A JSON Schema is published for editor autocompletion.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
The full guide lives in CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root. In short:

  • Setup: pip install -e ".[dev]" then pre-commit install.
  • Tests: pytest. Types: mypy src/. Lint: ruff check src/ tests/.
  • Sign your commits: git commit -s (Developer Certificate of Origin).
  • Add a news fragment: any user-visible change needs a file in changelog.d/ (see changelog.d/README.md).
  • Adding a rule: one rule module + a vulnerable fixture + a safe fixture + a docs page + registration in the category __init__.py.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
CodeGuard's exit code is a stable contract you can gate CI on.

Code Meaning 0 Completed; no findings (in v2.0: none at or above --fail-on, or --exit-zero was set). 1 Completed; one or more findings (in v2.0: at or above --fail-on). 2 Usage error — bad flag, unknown rule ID, unreadable path. 3 Config error — invalid codeguard.toml (v2.0). 4 Internal error — an unexpected exception (v2.0).

Today codes 3 and 4 are folded into 2. 0 and 1 are unchanged.

Suppressed findings never affect the exit code.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: The PyPI project is codeguard-cli. The installed command is codeguard.

docs.title: As a tool (recommended)
docs.text:
pipx install codeguard-cli
# or
uv tool install codeguard-cli

docs.title: Into an environment
docs.text:
pip install codeguard-cli

Requires Python 3.10 or newer. No database, no server, no network access at runtime.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/mevichitra/codeguard
cd codeguard
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pre-commit install

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
codeguard --version
codeguard scan .

docs.title: Other channels (v2.0)
docs.text: Docker image, standalone binaries, a Homebrew tap, a GitHub Action, and a .pre-commit-hooks.yaml land with v2.0. See CI integration.

docs.title: Migrating to v2
docs.text: v2.0 is a large step up from the 0.1 alpha. This page collects every backward-incompatible change so an upgrade is predictable. It is filled in as each change lands on main; see changelog.d/ for the in-flight set.

docs.title: Package renamed: codeguard → codeguard-cli
docs.text:
The bare codeguard name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. Install codeguard-cli instead:

pipx install codeguard-cli      # was: pipx install codeguard

The command (codeguard) and the import package (import codeguard) are unchanged. If you pinned codeguard in a requirements file, switch it to codeguard-cli.

docs.title: Planned (not yet on main)
docs.text: Change What to do Rule API check(tree, …) → analyze(ctx); languages attribute required Only affects custom rules. Built-in rules are cushioned by an AstRule base. Location.col becomes 1-indexed (was 0-indexed) Adjust any tooling that reads col from JSON output. SARIF column values are unaffected. --format json becomes an envelope object Parse .results instead of the top-level array, or use --format json-legacy for one more minor version. scan --severity splits into --fail-on (exit code) + display filter Use --fail-on in CI gates. --severity keeps working as a deprecated alias. Exit codes 3 (config) and 4 (internal) added 0 and 1 are unchanged; only broaden handling if you special-cased 2. Inline suppressions require reason: Add reason: … to each # codeguard: ignore[…]. Bare ones still suppress but raise CG-META-001. disable[…] → ignore-file[…] Rename at leisure; the old spelling stays as a deprecated alias. scan respects .gitignore + a built-in skip list by default Pass --no-gitignore to restore the previous breadth. SARIF partialFingerprints added GitHub code scanning re-keys existing alerts once on upgrade, then stays stable.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text: Select with --format.

docs.title: human (default)
docs.text: Coloured terminal output: one header line per finding (file:line:col [RULE] SEVERITY title), the offending source line with a caret, the fix suggestion, and a severity summary.

docs.title: json
docs.text:
A JSON array of finding objects. Each object has rule_id, title, description, severity, category, location (file, line, col, end_line, end_col), cwe, owasp, fix_suggestion, confidence, and suppressed.

Changing in v2.0

--format json becomes an envelope object — { version, tool, rules, results, summary } — with a per-finding fingerprint. The current bare-array output stays available as --format json-legacy for one minor version.

docs.title: sarif
docs.text:
SARIF 2.1.0 — the format GitHub code scanning and most analysis tooling understand. Includes a rules[] catalogue with CWE/OWASP metadata and, for suppressed findings, suppressions[] entries.

codeguard scan src/ --format sarif -o codeguard.sarif

Changing in v2.0

SARIF output gains partialFingerprints (stable across reformatting and line moves), security-severity, helpUri, and CWE taxonomy entries. v2.0 also adds github (Actions annotations), rdjson (reviewdog), and junit formats.

docs.title: Inline (one line)
docs.text:
query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {uid}"  # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-001]

Multiple rules on one line:

risky()  # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-001, CG-SEC-003]

docs.title: File-level
docs.text:
Anywhere in the file:

# codeguard: disable[CG-SEC-002]

docs.title: Visibility
docs.text:
Suppressed findings are not lost. They appear with --show-suppressed, as "suppressed": true in JSON, and as suppressions[] entries in SARIF, so suppression usage can be audited.

Changing in v2.0

Suppressions gain a mandatory reason: (a bare suppression still works but raises CG-META-001), an optional until=YYYY-MM-DD expiry (CG-META-002 once expired), per-language comment syntax (// for JS/TS), and a codeguard suppressions list --expired command. disable[…] is renamed to ignore-file[…] (old spelling kept as a deprecated alias).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
codeguard scan PATH

PATH is a file or a directory (scanned recursively for *.py).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Description --format {human,json,sarif} Output format. Default human. --rule RULE_ID Only run the named rule(s). Repeatable. Validated against the registry. --severity {critical,high,medium,low,info} Only report findings at or above this level. --show-suppressed Include suppressed findings in the output. -o, --output PATH Write output to a file instead of stdout.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
codeguard scan src/
codeguard scan auth.py --format json
codeguard scan src/ --format sarif -o results.sarif
codeguard scan . --rule CG-SEC-001 --rule CG-SEC-002
codeguard scan . --severity high

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
0 no findings · 1 findings · 2 error. Full contract in Exit codes.

Changing in v2.0

v2.0 adds codeguard ci, baseline, list-rules, explain, validate, and init commands, a config file, --fail-on / --diff / --baseline / --jobs / --exclude flags, stdin input, and .gitignore-aware discovery. --severity becomes a display filter and --fail-on controls the exit code.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Every rule has a stable ID (CG-<CATEGORY>-<NNN>), a severity, a CWE/OWASP mapping, and a fix suggestion. IDs are permanent — never renumbered or reused.

ID Title Severity Category CWE Languages CG-SEC-001 SQL query built with string formatting HIGH security CWE-89 Python CG-SEC-002 Hardcoded secret HIGH security CWE-798 Python CG-SEC-003 eval() / exec() on dynamic input HIGH security CWE-95 Python CG-SEC-004 Unsafe deserialization HIGH security CWE-502 Python CG-SEC-005 subprocess with shell=True and a dynamic command HIGH security CWE-78 Python

v2.0

This table will be generated from rule metadata (the same source codeguard explain <ID> reads), with a page per rule covering rationale, examples, false positives, and suppression. JavaScript and TypeScript rules join the list.

List rules from the CLI:

codeguard --version   # today
codeguard list-rules  # v2.0

docs.title: CG-SEC-001: SQL Injection via String Formatting
Description
docs.text: Detects SQL queries constructed using f-strings, .format(), or % string formatting with user-controlled input. This allows attackers to manipulate the query logic, bypass authentication, or exfiltrate data.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-89 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
  • OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
def get_user(uid):
    query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {uid}"
    cursor.execute(query)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
def get_user(uid):
    cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (uid,))

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Always use parameterized queries or prepared statements. Never concatenate or interpolate user input directly into SQL strings.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, and secrets assigned directly to variables. Hardcoded credentials embedded in source code can be exposed via version control history or code leaks.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-798 — Use of Hard-coded Credentials
  • OWASP: A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
api_key = "sk-abc123xyz"
password = "supersecret123"

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import os
api_key = os.environ.get("API_KEY")
password = os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD")

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Load secrets from environment variables, a secrets manager (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault), or a .env file that is excluded from version control.

docs.title: CG-SEC-003: Use of eval() or exec()
Description
docs.text: Detects calls to eval() or exec() with dynamic or user-controlled input. These functions execute arbitrary Python code and can be exploited to run malicious commands on the server.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-95 — Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
  • OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
user_input = input("Enter expression: ")
result = eval(user_input)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import ast
result = ast.literal_eval(user_input)  # Only safe for literals

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Avoid eval() and exec() entirely. Use ast.literal_eval() for safe literal parsing, or redesign the logic to avoid dynamic code execution.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Detects use of pickle.loads() on untrusted data or yaml.load() without SafeLoader. Deserializing untrusted data with these functions can lead to arbitrary code execution.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-502 — Deserialization of Untrusted Data
  • OWASP: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
import pickle
obj = pickle.loads(data_from_network)

import yaml
config = yaml.load(file_content)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import yaml
config = yaml.safe_load(file_content)

import json
data = json.loads(file_content)  # prefer JSON over pickle

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Never unpickle data from untrusted sources. Use yaml.safe_load() instead of yaml.load(). Prefer JSON or other safe formats for data exchange.

docs.title: CG-SEC-005: subprocess with shell=True and Variable Input
Description
docs.text: Detects calls to subprocess.run(), subprocess.call(), or subprocess.Popen() with shell=True and a dynamic (non-literal) command string. This can allow command injection if user input reaches the command.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-78 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
  • OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
import subprocess
filename = input("Enter filename: ")
subprocess.run(f"cat {filename}", shell=True)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["cat", filename])  # list form, no shell

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Pass commands as a list instead of a string to avoid shell interpretation. If shell=True is required, ensure the command string is fully static and never includes user-controlled input.
